text:
IncidentBot: paging: SLO breach detected — p99 streaming tail latency >1200ms for model-inference-prod in eu-west-2. Auto-alert threshold hit at 2026-03-15T02:08:00Z. Paging oncall group @oncall-rotate :rotating_light:

oncall-rotate: ack — I'm up. grabbing dashboards.

cheng: I'm seeing a simultaneous spike in TLS handshake errors and retransmits across azb/azc in eu-west-2. p95 is up ~300ms but p99 is 1.2-1.6s. Packet loss counters jump at 02:06:xx.

alex: copying graphs — real-time: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/streams?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-2 (send to SRE dashboard).

oncall-rotate: quick checks — netstat on a few inference hosts? any conntrack saturations?

cheng: running quick conntrack check on rwi-infer-eu-a-02: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` shows ~88k entries, threshold 100k but growth rate high. Also `ss -s` shows high retransmit.

liam: I see NAT gateway logs showing many ephemeral port exhaustion warnings in the same timeframe. NAT rotation/ephemeral allocations spike. Could be backend egress path.

eva: customer-facing metric: streaming sessions with stalls jumped 11% for affected tenants. PMs pinged. pm_jordan — what's our external comms?

pm_jordan: hold — need impact estimate first. which customers had degraded streams vs total?

cheng: quick breakdown: 3% of overall requests in eu-west-2 experienced >1s tail; for customers on dedicated pools behind the eu-nat path it's ~9%.

oncall-rotate: mitigation proposal: 1) enable region fallback route for streaming (route policy delta) 2) drain NAT-heavy nodes, add temporary egress nodes from standby pool 3) add TLS handshake retry backoff tweak on proxy layer. Which one can we action quickly?

alex: I can push the route policy change now to divert traffic to eu-west-1 for non-low-latency tenants. Command: `rbctl routing apply --policy fallback-eu-west1 --selector streaming=best-effort` — doing a dry-run then apply.

cheng: while Alex applies, I'm going to rotate NAT gateways in eu-west-2: `aws ec2 replace-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id nat-0abcd` (we have warm spare NGWs). I'll do one AZ at a time.

oncall-rotate: ok do small batches. also enable extended logging on TLS proxy: `proxyctl debug tls-handshake --level=info --since=5m`

liam: spinning up two extra egress instances from reserved pool now (rwi-egress-standby-*). ETA ~90s.

alex: route change applied (dry-run good) -> applying now. Watching streaming ingress metrics.

IncidentBot: change deployed by alex at 02:11:42Z: routing policy fallback-eu-west1 applied to selector streaming=best-effort.

cheng: nat rotation started for azc. one gateway replaced, ephemeral port usage dropped after rotation for that AZ. Retransmits down ~30%.

eva: observing streaming stalls % drop to ~4% in affected cohorts. p99 trending down to ~700-800ms now.

pm_jordan: good. Prepare an interim status for customers: affected customers in dedicated pools experienced degraded streaming for ~6 minutes; most traffic successfully rerouted; mitigation in progress. I'll draft msg once we have stable p99 under target.

oncall-rotate: monitoring for 10m. If stable, we'll close paging and start incident triage. Otherwise escalate to network infra owners.

cheng: note — TLS handshake error histogram shows a particular client-side cipher negotiation that fails more after NAT port remap. Might be related to stale NAT translation. Will capture pcaps from nginx-proxy a-02 for 02:04-02:10.

liam: added extra NLB capacity and egress instances are healthy. No CPU/memory pressure.

alex: rolling back route change is simple if needed: `rbctl routing rollback last --selector streaming=best-effort`. Keep that ready.

IncidentBot: alert suppressed automatically at 02:17:30Z as p99 < threshold for 5m.

oncall-rotate: marking incident as mitigated for paging purposes. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes.

pm_jordan: drafting customer note: short cause + mitigation + ETA for postmortem. Will ask SRE for preliminary root-cause hypothesis.

cheng: preliminary RCA note: transient NAT port exhaustion and high retransmit rates in eu-west-2 due to a burst of upstream egress flows causing increased TLS handshake latency; NAT replacement + egress scaling + routing fallback reduced tail latency. Need deeper look at upstream client behavior and ephemeral port allocation policies.

oncall-rotate: action items assigned: 
- cheng: collect pcaps, NAT gateway flow logs, and conntrack deltas (due EOD)
- liam: run capacity test on NAT + NLB to reproduce in staging (due tomorrow)
- alex: add automated fallback route unit test to prevent config drift (due next week)
- eva + pm_jordan: customer comms + impact receipts (send within 1h)

pm_jordan: thanks — will coordinate.

oncall-rotate: handing off to night oncall @cheng for follow-up, I will update incident board and set severity to Sev3 for formal triage. If anything blips tonight ping #onduty.

cheng: ack handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and start the log collection.

alex: raw commands run during mitigation for audit: ```
rbctl routing apply --policy fallback-eu-west1 --selector streaming=best-effort
aws ec2 replace-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id nat-0abcd --region eu-west-2
proxyctl debug tls-handshake --level=info --since=5m
kubectl get pods -l app=stream-proxy -n inference -o wide
```

eva: saved screenshots of dashboards and will attach to incident board. customers notified: "We're aware of streaming stalls in eu-west-2; mitigation applied; investigating root cause.", pending final postmortem.

pm_jordan: final note for now — estimated customer impact window 02:04:00Z–02:12:30Z, ~8.5 minutes. Affected fraction: 3% overall in eu-west-2, up to 9% for some dedicated setups. Will update thread when root cause confirmed.

oncall-rotate: closing active paging — switching to post-incident triage. Great cross-team response, thanks everyone :pray:
